Its compact body has soft grey-brown hairlike fibres. Its long low narrow toothed beak and smooth rounded crown follow the fossil reference. Both thin leathery wings are folded neatly along its body, with two small feet resting naturally on the rock. A long thin straight tail extends horizontally behind the body and ends in a small diamond-shaped membrane, clearly separated from the folded wings. The entire animal and tail are visible in side profile. Soft brown and grey natural animal colours. Pale limestone occupies the near lower third, softly defocused turquoise lagoon, sea-green night sky and a small coral-pink moon lie behind. Neutral documentary fill reveals the beak, folded wings, feet and tail, a subtle warm moon reflection touches the stone. premise.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 2, because the drying lagoons left sticky mud that trapped insects and small dinosaurs. Stay on firm ground.

fact.text: The Solnhofen lagoons at times almost dried out, exposing sticky carbonate mud that trapped insects and a few small dinosaurs.
fact.source_sentence: At times, the lagoons almost dried out, exposing sticky carbonate muds that trapped insects and a few small dinosaurs.

premise.description:
A Late Jurassic island chain in what is now Germany, with warm lagoons that look perfect for the night. Eight choices, from a conifer ridge to a swim in open water.

Head geometry reference: Rhamphorhynchus specimen from Solnhofen, photo Dean Falk Schnabel, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rhamphorhynchus_muensteri_fossil.jpg, CC0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), cropped fossil reference used for AI adaptation, living animal, colour and setting are illustrative.

Drifting on a big driftwood log. Dead centre of the dried lagoon mud. Wading out to the sponge reef. Swimming to the next island at night.
